I will keep the full 50 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best, it fits my land and well irrigation, and after 30 years I trust it more than changing crops. With some family labor working off-farm, I will keep management practical and steady rather than overly intensive. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer in as a solid base with enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, and irrigate a few key times because water is available from the well but still costs money and labor. I will use rotary tillage after maize because it is faster and suits my scale. For summer maize, I will also stay with improved high-yield seed, use moderate fertilizer with nitrogen as the main driver, and keep irrigation to the critical periods if rainfall is short. I will spray pesticides only when needed, but I will still plan a few applications because weeds, aphids, and common field diseases usually show up in a normal year here. I am aiming for stable yield and manageable cost, not the most aggressive input level.
